notes.title: I MADE A SONG for my INDIE GAME!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=Gk0lzLnZ4wE;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]I like games and music. [/h2]
You'd probably say "wow, it's like... 99% of the world population". Nah, I LIKE, LIKE games and music. I enjoy them so much, I even decided to make my own games. Aaaaand, you know, it's been... tough (!), but I didn't quit (yet) and instead, I sat over my desk and thought... and thought, and thought again, AND THEN I got to the idea of making my own superhero series! Listen, I love Batman, alright? Hell, who doesn’t love Batman! I was always watching new episodes of Batman Beyond as a kid and those are the best memories of my childhood.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44551684/b1af21a70fc05183d0a3569b53b696a86690d9b7.gif[/img]

So together with my friend Witek, we decided to really dedicate ourselves to that project and firstly - we made a free game called Hank: Straightjacket. It was… quite nice, but it was tiny, so the next step was to create something bigger, greater, more exciting and world changing (yeah I’m exaggerating a bit). The thing was - we didn’t know how to make it more… I don’t know, distinctive? iconic? So… we made a song!

https://youtu.be/lxFqR0UQG1Q?si=5oturWNEW8XFxYUx

[h2]Designing characters[/h2]
But at first we had to design the characters - our main guy is Hank. He’s not your typical superhero with lots of money or a pretty face, in fact, he’s an alcoholic who many years ago was a master in street fighting at an underground arena. But one day his entire life fell off, he got drunk to death and when he woke up with a crazy hangover, he realised that he came in possession of a time travelling superpowers. There’s also his nemesis, Unraveler, the greatest illusionist this world has known, and many other characters but I won’t spoil too much, y-you have to try my game to learn more!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44551684/3967b09a17d1d4c3d506669c59dd4afce4463af6.png[/img]

But yeah, that’s basically the game, Unraveler poisoned Hank and took him into his world of illusion and now Hank has to escape, that’s the plot of Hank: Drowning On Dry Land. And although we know that all of this is cool and fun, we felt like there’s something missing. So we went back to watching Batman: Beyond, watched all the episodes for 10 times each and… nothing. We were slamming our heads against the wall and couldn’t come with the answer to our question: what is missing? And after days and nights with no sleep, tired and absolutely depressed, IN JUST ONE MOMENT we looked at eachother with Witek with that spark in our eyes and both said: THE SONG!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44551684/9a5bb228f51f51daef12d6633e8252c762986e8c.png[/img]

[h2]The song[/h2]
That was it! Every superhero has a theme song! And Hank also has to have one! We found the band that we thought would perfectly match the rock aesthetic we had in mind, guys are called Cinemon (you can check them out if you want) and we all were super excited to collaborate, so… we started working on it. It wasn’t a quick process, but let me tell you, the final result exceeded our wildest expectations. This raw, rock, grunge aesthetic is exactly what we were looking for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44551684/26ec8cc83fe22358f7e417fff864264ca456e6e9.gif[/img]

The full song is already available at Cinemon’s youtube channel with a dedicated lyric video, you’ll find a link to it a bit higher in this article, a link to Hank: Drowning On Dry Land game on Steam is below. Go check it out, aaaand see you… in the nightmares!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1937880/Hank_Drowning_On_Dry_Land/

notes.title: Our crew is getting bigger!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey hey hey, there's a new pirate on this ship![/h2]

My name is [b]Mateusz[/b] and for two months now I've been helping [b]Kuba[/b] and [b]Witek[/b] with their social media. Who am I exactly, how would I describe working with the [b]My Next Games[/b] team and what are our plans for the future?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42195882/37d19fb0490373403e35e81a1ace6f44657363f9.png[/img]

I have been running my YouTube channel for quite some time now and my content is mainly about [i][b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b][/i] from[b] CD Projekt RED[/b]. Making videos has been my hobby since I remember and I can hardly imagine anything else that gives me the same amount of joy. Besides that I'm also [i]a self-taught Photoshop editor[/i]. I learned that skill because I couldn't stand my awful thumbnails on YouTube anymore, haha. But seriously, a couple years ago I had to choose: do I want to become an IT specialist or a graphic designer. I picked the first one and as time runs I think that I could've picked the second option.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42195882/b848d173f4fef74fe702d06fee1e807dcff6300f.gif[/img]

[b]But hey, humans learn their whole lives, right?[/b] And after a consideration it's not even that bad, because now if I would like to have my own website, thanks to my IT skills from school I can make one by myself, while the rest of my graphic design skills I learned on my own. I consider this as an absolute win! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42195882/27aee5cbd6125627ea923d9573d3e51109f15260.jpg[/img]

My other hobby is Video Games. [b]That's why I decided to team-up with Kuba and Witek from My Next Games.[/b] The goal was simple - they make fun games and I use my experience to help them with the recognition of their series on the internet. We started very simply - they showed me their games, which by the way I really liked, especially the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1937880/Hank_Drowning_On_Dry_Land/]Hank[/url] one, and then I proceeded to think about new content for social media. At first on our [b]Facebook, TikTok, Instagram[/b] etc. you could see just usual posts about our games. Nothing special. Then we extended our content to include articles and now we’ve just started with full YouTube videos.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42195882/d22f1c2c87b873b03a951b82360c52483274a413.png[/img]

And here we are today. We just released our first video, which you can find on our [url=https://www.youtube.com/@Mynextgames]YouTube channel[/url]. It’s a summary of all upcoming [b]Indie Games[/b] that were presented at this year’s [b]The Game Awards[/b]. We invite you to check it out and to tell us in the comments what you like the most about this video and maybe what you don’t like about it. We’ll be very grateful.

[b]Be with us on this journey and help us make better and better content for you. See you around![/b]

notes.title: Full Dead Horizon adventure game demo now playable!
notes.content:
Hey Everybody!

Kuba from My Next Games here. For few years now I've been helping my friend Matthew to bring to life his vision for a game. We finaly have somthing we would like to share with you. I'm not that good with words so let me just pass it on to Matt:

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1368540/Dead_Horizon/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26308370/a2a10103690f4e083dbd3d33cc63e3cfe3ab7336.png[/img][/url]

Greetings fellow shootists!

Over the years a lot of people have told me that if there was a more fleshed out version of a game I made. It was a short adventure game that is about ten minutes long. People liked it but they wanted something with you know... more... game in it.

I have been working on a more fleshed out version of that other game for a few years. Now I have a demo to show off!

The demo was supposed to be shown off in the steamfest this week, but...

Well, I am also sometimes an idiot. I messed up the submission process twice so instead... the demo is going to be available next week! I'll have my OWN Steamfest! It won't have blackjack or hookers but it will have the (Still slightly janky) demo for Dead Horizon: The Longer Version!

This game will be a full adventure game with point and click stuff going on. An inventory. It includes...
[list]
[*] The ability to talk to people.
[*] The ability to shoot people.
[*] An inventory.
[*] A lot of niche and optional content most people will never see because sometimes late at night I can't sleep and I just go write long conversations
[*] The ability to look at things and get descriptions of them!
[*] No voice acting!
[*] Being slightly unfinished. SFX especially need a touch more work.
[*] An obvious representation of my psyche an world view in video game form.
[*] A weird sci0fi western setting that seems to be a normal western setting at first but if you read way too many of the buried look ats you realize 'wait what?!' and then you are like 'oh, okay' and then you're like 'huh, maybe he should have made this more obvious?'
[*] Years of blood and sweat soaked into the code and pixels in a desperate attempt to hold onto my nostalgia of the 90s.
[*] Ability to shoot someone's hat off their head.
[*] Pixel art that is really really keeno!
[*] Play as a drunk!
[*] Freak people out by pulling your gun out randomly mid conversation.
[*] Um... there's other stuff. I think.
[/list]

It's something you can check out right now. You can play it over here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1368540/Dead_Horizon/

The demo will be up and playable for a week or so. Feel free to play it, wishlist it, tell people about it, make fun of it, hate it, or whatever. I mean, I can't control you. You seem like an independent and smart minded person if you've reading this update, and you know what? I trust you.

You'll probably get what I'm trying to build here.

Feel free to tell me if I am missing the mark! This is a demo meaning that feedback at this stage is fantabulous.

I hope all of you find what you are looking for out in the shifting sands.

-Always

Matthew Ritter

notes.title: Soulblight at Chinajoy
notes.content:
Hello Everybody
Kuba from My Next Games here. How's it going? Today I would like to tell you about our recent trip to Chinajoy.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/daacacebd0c457aa38695da569c91f7deb91c962.jpg[/img]
It all started very suddenly when we've been contacted by people from Foundation Indie Games Poland (IGP). They've asked us if we would be interested in becoming a part of the Polish Game Stand at Chinajoy this years. To be honest I was a bit surprised. I knew the event was in just one week but we weren't planing on participating. We didn't even apply for the IGP recruitment for it. The representative of IGP explained that one of the games that was supposed to participate dropped out on the last minute and that they are looking for a replacement. As Soulblight was already a part of the IGP Stand at PAX West Seattle twice they though that it would be a good game to showcase in China as well :D.

I've never been to China so I said - Let's do it!:D
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/cfa54cef36d6690f2c447fe8e7b9a39435510a23.png[/img]
[h1]Day 1[/h1]
After a week of intensive preparations and over 12h flight we landed in Shanghai. The airport looked like a regular European airport only bigger. The first noticeable difference was the wave of heat that struck us when we left the building. We were very glad that our hotel seemed to be not too far. We soon realized it wasn't exactly true. Taxi trip took us almost 45 minutes! It looks like everything is bigger and further away here. The rest of the day we spend sleeping of the trip.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/dda7669579bb4b044d3fc92e99897c391484c5dc.jpg[/img]
[h1]Day 2[/h1]
After good 12h sleep we woke up at 10 A.M. The Chinajoy was still one day away so we decided to spend the day sight seeing and getting acquainted with original chines food ;) 
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/c574acad987772ae2b2e20769a3532f9718d81f6.jpg[/img]
[h1]Day 3[/h1]
The first day of the event. We woke up at 6 A.M so we can get to the venue earlier and set up the stand. Here's how it looked like:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/3299fa3d0a408af7770841cc64fcacf11840dcf7.jpg[/img]
After the event we went for the Polish party organized by IGP and Polish Institute in Beijing. We didn't realize that It took place in fancy five star hotel. When we got to the sight we felt a bit under-dressed wearing our regular cloths. Fortunately when guests started to arrive the feeling disappeared. The party was specifically designed to promote Polish games. There were even a dedicated stations provided by the organizers with our games so the guest can check them out.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/52e5dac7fdb6d31c1251275900247c1b85f63e2c.jpg[/img]
[h1]Day 4[/h1]
The second day of the event. Today we decided to get to the venue by subway. We didn't realize we'er going to travel during the rush hour. It was so crowded that despite all the air-conditioning and ventilation it was still hard to breath. Fortunately the Subway is very efficient and we were able to get to Chinajoy without any delay.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/1a6040d03e3c078a0c13529f7a6ed54cdc04c3a0.jpg[/img]
After the second day of the event we got invited to the party organized by Sina Games. It took place in an exclusive Light Club in the city center. The Club itself had this awesome cyberpunky feel to it.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/51a353960c0fc10d0ae4ceb90f2cfa5184abf2ac.jpg[/img]
[h1]Day 5[/h1]
As usually on this kind of events the last day was a bit slower. We got to the stand 15 minutes late but fortunately at the business section people started to show up that day an hour later. Evening that day we decided to take a bit slower as well. We went for a little evening stroll by the river.

notes.title: Taint Room Progression
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/8f8e8b33b7ba482ae7498110d36c1cea4ab976ac.gif[/img]
Hey Everybody - Happy Easters!
Yup! The new Soulblight update is now live. When you launch the game you might noticed the following things:
[list]
    [*]Taints are now randomly assigned to the path  
    [*]Not all taint room paths are unlocked from the start
[/list]
What we've realized during last couple of weeks was that allowing player to chose from all 4 taints every level actually decreased the replay value of our game. After few runs everybody has a favorite setup and stops experimenting with other available option. Yes - randomly assigning taints to the path and adding a lot of new taints would have solved the problem. Although we plan on adding new personalities it will take some time and we thought this problem couldn't wait that long. On the other hand some of you mentioned the game could use some additional progression mechanics. And so the idea pop into our minds - we've decided to kill two birds with a one stone :)

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/6be57dfd77cbff68e91b4f7e4fbb89246aafbc41.gif[/img]

Now at the start of the game only two paths with random taints will be available. This way you will no longer be able to use the same taint setup in every game. To get access to additional choice options you will need to unlock the other paths. You do it with Corrupted Cores. Every time you defeat the boss you will get one Corrupted Core. Power up the taint room with 3 of thous and a new path will open :)

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/aeed26a38bd23d2b8f55e335d901cd160ce53aa3.gif[/img]

To add even more depth to taint selection we've also introduced to the game a less powerful version of the core. The Energy Core will alow you to re-role one of the taint options and it is now available to buy at Cecil's Dungeon Crawling Paraphernalia Emporium ;)

Cya Around,
Kuba

notes.title: Kickstarter Update 5#: Character’s Conditions
notes.content:
As you can see today we have another extensive topic :) Let’s just jump straight into it :)

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/8ed984c2ae1b044bc5a854985ec72951e237b86a.png[/img] 

One of the early design challenges during the development of Soulblight was creating a context for all the action the player would have to take in order express his characters. To solve that we’ve decided to add a survival aspect to our game. We’ve done it by allowing the character to be a subject of various conditions. To avoid confusion and allow the player to easily compare buffs he receives we’ve created a special state called synergy. What it does is it represents the character’s overall well being (both physical and psychic) and greatly increases damage and resistance. To systemize the mechanics even further we’ve also divided the conditions into 4 categories:

[list]
[*][b]Positive Conditions[/b] - Simple buffs meant to make you stronger by temporarily increasing the synergy. Example: Rage
[*][b]Negative Conditions[/b] -Simple debuffs that won’t kill you but make you weaker by decreasing your synergy. Example: Hunger
[*][b]Injuries[/b] - Serious wounds. With every one of these you get closer and closer to death. You can sustain up to 4 Injuries at the same time. Example: Bleeding wound
[*][b]Taints[/b] - The personality traits you acquire during your journey besides giving you a passive synergy buff also unlock a new mechanics. Example: Greed 
[/list]

Now the fun part starts when the different conditions start to intertwine. Let’s look at hunger example:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/ecb5eccbd53ba08d71ebb1697d6f2a92a9061106.png[/img]

The hunger builds up with the time you play. It starts as a small harmless debuf but can build up to enormous proportion. That’s why It is important to eat regularly especially when you have a concussion injury (it will speed up the healing process). Saving candies for later might be a good idea but their nutritional value isn’t too high. This means that a piece of candy will nullify the hunger just for a short time. notes.title: Kickstarter Update 5#: Character’s Conditions
notes.content:
As you can see today we have another extensive topic :) Let’s just jump straight into it :)

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/8ed984c2ae1b044bc5a854985ec72951e237b86a.png[/img] 

One of the early design challenges during the development of Soulblight was creating a context for all the action the player would have to take in order express his characters. To solve that we’ve decided to add a survival aspect to our game. We’ve done it by allowing the character to be a subject of various conditions. To avoid confusion and allow the player to easily compare buffs he receives we’ve created a special state called synergy. What it does is it represents the character’s overall well being (both physical and psychic) and greatly increases damage and resistance. To systemize the mechanics even further we’ve also divided the conditions into 4 categories:

[list]
[*][b]Positive Conditions[/b] - Simple buffs meant to make you stronger by temporarily increasing the synergy. Example: Rage
[*][b]Negative Conditions[/b] -Simple debuffs that won’t kill you but make you weaker by decreasing your synergy. Example: Hunger
[*][b]Injuries[/b] - Serious wounds. With every one of these you get closer and closer to death. You can sustain up to 4 Injuries at the same time. Example: Bleeding wound
[*][b]Taints[/b] - The personality traits you acquire during your journey besides giving you a passive synergy buff also unlock a new mechanics. Example: Greed 
[/list]

notes.title: Kickstarter Update 4#: Challenges of Top-Down View
notes.content:
Top-down perspective has multiple advantages. It allows to represent battlefield precisely, players can clearly see obstacles arrangement and distance from enemies. This view emphasizes tactical oriented combat and supports sneaking mechanics.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/700c1068b049505dd4a09c043fcb6b202a472d77.png[/img]
Despite all that, top-down is rarely used in video games. The reason is a difficulty in presenting the in-game world. There are many objects that don’t look presentable in top-down. Their geometry doesn’t allow to give us much chance to properly display them. In front view a simple wall is like a canvas on which we literally can put an intriguing painting on, but in top-down - it comes out as a line. To make things even more difficult there is also an issue with a lack of depth.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/e06f233fc08eb6f7b31058e2bd1c95d5bc635a0e.jpg[/img]
From the very beginning we were dedicated to solving those problems. We didn’t want to give up on all the benefits of top-down just because it was hard. We subconsciously started to design assets with interesting appearance in our perspective. Bridges rather than gates. Pits of pipes in place of columns. Flowery shrubs instead of walls. All of this led us to the unique art style of our game.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/d8a6bf5969d301a2f2e5d73e040315dd5da474fe.gif[/img]
There still was a problem with sense of depth thought. We solved it with parallaxing effect you’ve all seen on backgrounds in platform games. Assets are constructed from multiple layers which are slightly displaced depending of the camera position. Combined together they create an illusion of convexity like on the gif below

notes.title: Kickstarter Update 3#: Why Top-Down?
notes.content:
What we’re often asked is:

[b][i]“Why did you choose pure top-down perspective instead of for example an isometric view?”[/i][/b]

Answer to this question is quite complex :) But here's a short take on the thought process behind our decision:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/b66527c1ecf08afeca3be10d19210acc1ec0d97e.png[/img]
Creating a game in which you can express states of character psyche requires designing many different interactions and mechanic through which you can do it. To be able to do everything we want in isometric view we basically would have to create everything in 3D. Unfortunately this takes much more time. The level of gameplay depth we strived for would be very hard to achieve in 3D by the small team like ours. We knew it would most likely mean that we have to either simplify the game or compromise the quality of our art.

[b][i]“If not isometric, then how about side-view”[/i][/b]

The problem here was a combat mechanic we’ve chosen for Soulblight. We didn’t want for our game to be about button mashing. What we wanted is for the player to always think one step ahead while fighting. Because battlefield positioning was supposed to be a big part of tactics we felt that “Platformer” view limited a bit too much what we could do.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/9655ad9a2ea05bce5ef19be5c9880607621ca5ea.jpg[/img]
And so we’ve decided to go with a top-down view. It is the best way to present to player situation on the battlefield. On top of that top-down perspective works well with sneaking mechanic that we wanted to include in the game. This didn’t mean there were no challenges ahead. On a contrary there are reasons why this perspective isn’t a popular choice among the developers. We had a few ideas how to tackle those problems though. What were they and how we solved them? Well... this is a topic for another update :)

Cya Around,
Kuba

notes.title: Kickstarter Update 2#: The Nuances Of Sneaking
notes.content:
After an update on combat it’s time for the one about sneaking. We design stealth in Soulblight to be complementary to fighting. This means that when properly used in combination with fighting it will give you a huge advantage.

The challenge starts when you bump into squeaking terrain like old wooden footbridge - here every step will make a noise. To mitigate that you will have to move even slower with gentle use of the analog stick.

notes.title: Kickstarter Update 1#: Combat Tactics
notes.content:
Hey Everybody!
It's time for our first Kickstarter update. Today I would like to talk in more detail about combat in Soulblight. Before we go any further you need to know one thing about me. I’m a martial art enthusiast :) As a programmer and game designer I spend most of my days in a dark room in front of the screen :P This way of life isn’t too healthy so to balance things out I train Judo. You don't believe me? Here's a gif of me (barely) performing a throw :P
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/9b7621845f92e66bdc9b674f7b245f99056771b1.gif[/img]
The thing I love the most about fighting is the fact that what matters the most is not the strength but tactics. This is a different kind of tactics than you know from strategy game though. It’s more like thinking about the plan under the pressure of things happening right here and now. This is what I wanted for our combat mechanic to be all about. In my experience tactics in martial arts consists of the following elements:
[list]
[*]Management of Strength
[*]Distance Control
[*]Balance Control
[/list]
Now let’s talk in more detail about those elements and see how they are represented in our game mechanics.

[h1] Management of Strength[/h1]
You have to be careful not to use use all of your strength during the fight. If you do, you will run out of steam very fast and will be easy overwhelmed. The tactics here is about finding the right moment to catch your breath. This element of fighting has been pretty well represented in gaming through the years by the stamina mechanics. I’ve decided for it to be a base of combat in Soulblight
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/d71d81f2a4f0a82df7c53041f9e3b755f59afa83.gif[/img]

[h1]Distance Control[/h1]
Though stamina management was a relatively obvious thing the same couldn’t be said about the distance control. Video games often do away with clinch combat. This results in removing a lot of tactical depth. Suddenly everything boils down to your attack speed and power. Meanwhile in reality a double handed sword isn’t nearly as useful up close as from afar. When you engage an enemy wielding a heavy weapon he cannot keep swinging while in clinch - he needs to find a way to disengage. To represent this I’ve decided to create a grip mechanic.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/c4701942fda08b2bb7f0a0f9ac9d2f0dfd97fc82.gif[/img]
During combat each character is surrounded by a circle which represent its position on the battlefield. By pressing the button you can light up a front part of it and activate what we call “the grip”. When your grip touches your opponents circle the characters become engaged in clinch combat. This maneuver, besides linking the characters together, also forces them to use a secondary attack. Depending on the weapon this attack might be less or more powerful than the main one. The one who wields a more cumbersome weapon now will be forced to find a way to disengage. The easiest way to do it is by performing a special “slam” action. But be careful this maneuver burns a lot of stamina.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/4312691b27be086fb62c3c92910904596e3711f8.gif[/img]

[h1]Balance Control[/h1]
Ok this part of the mechanics is explicitly linked to the martial art I’m training :). Judo is focusing on the clinch combat and can be translated as “The path of the least resistance”. The idea is that while engaged you need to move in a way to throw your enemy of balance so you can use much less strength to defeat him. How this idea is implemented in Soulblight? - you ask. When engaged you cannot move away from the enemy but you can move around him. By implementing certain level of inertia depending on how well armored your character is we’ve allowed the faster character to be able to outmaneuver the heavier foes. This way you can get on the back of the heavier opponents and gain a massive advantage. Although it isn’t easy it greatly increases your damage as well as prevents the enemy from hitting you with his attacks.
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/6f6aaac4796a82c1520ead6c03e7809cff1adb14.gif[/img]
The combat in Soulblight might look a bit Hack & Slashy at first glance but the truth is button mashing won’t get you far. If you have any questions feel free to ask them in a comment section :) And don't forget to visit our kickstarter page:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/1752350052/soulblight

Cya around,
Kuba

notes.title: Soulblight Kickstarter - OCT 17th
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/9ca90e1a54de7573fe19a711e449c5369a2d6733.png[/img]

Hey Everybody!
As you know last month we’ve decided to delay our Kickstarter campaign in order to spend more time polishing it. Since then we’ve been working very hard and this time I’ve decided not to mention anything about it until we were 100% satisfied with our pitch. And now, since we are, the time has come to finally announce it - [b]Soulblight Kickstarter campaign will go live on October 17th[/b] ( btw it just so happens that it’s just one day after my birthday ;) )

Now let's talk a bit about some of the improvements we’ve made to the campaign:

[h1]Demo[/h1]
First of all to reward you for waiting we've decided to add a demo access as an additional Kickstarter reward! :) We will send out the demo keys just after the end of the campaign! So if you decide to become our backer you will be able to try out Soulblight really soon!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/d16bd87eb8e16bbd309bfaa36035b5223c91e8e1.png[/img]

[h1]New Main Message[/h1]
One of the main reasons for postponing Kickstarter was the fact that our “More literal approach to RPG” pitch was a bit too abstract to get across without at least two paragraphs of text. However removing this aspect from the game to make it more “promotable” was absolutely out of the question. The only solution was finding a new way of talking about our game. The answer came to us at PAX West. While chatting with all the people visiting our stand we’ve realized that we’ve been focusing on a wrong thing in our pitch. Instead of talking about game’s mechanics we should be emphasizing what we’re actually trying to say with it.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/16cf450b094c60d9f06282e6b424acded5ed2f34.png[/img]

Probably some of you already know what I’m talking about :). The question: [i]“Why the personalities you can acquire in the game are always negative?”[/i] was popping out quite regularly. It was natural as all the little signs were already there:
[list]
[*]The name of the game - “Soulblight” suggest that it’s about the sickness of the soul
[*]The quote form “The Divine Comedy” in the trailer pointed in this direction as well
[*]Our main art presenting that the greatest danger in the game will come “from behind you”
[*]The fact that we chose to call progression system in the game “Taining Mechanic” was also a hint
[/list]
All this was already there. What was lacking were three sentences with which we could explain all that to the person that knows absolutely nothing about the game. (btw never thought writing 3 sentences can be that hard) And so here it is:

[b][i]Soulblight is a dark, top-down roguelike luring you to cross the thin line between good and evil. Embrace your flaws to survive a journey through an unforgiving Sanctuary. Gluttony, Lust, Cannibalism - how far are you willing to go?[/i][/b]

[h1]New Main Art[/h1]
Another thing we’ve addressed was our main art. It wasn’t that we weren't satisfied with the one we had. On the contrary we really liked how straightforward it presented the top down perspective and at the same time shown the danger of Soulblight lurking behind the character. The thing that we considered a problem was the fact that once you scaled it down its readability dropped drastically. notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/9ca90e1a54de7573fe19a711e449c5369a2d6733.png[/img]

Hey Everybody!
As you know last month we’ve decided to delay our Kickstarter campaign in order to spend more time polishing it. Since then we’ve been working very hard and this time I’ve decided not to mention anything about it until we were 100% satisfied with our pitch. And now, since we are, the time has come to finally announce it - [b]Soulblight Kickstarter campaign will go live on October 17th[/b] ( btw it just so happens that it’s just one day after my birthday ;) )

Now let's talk a bit about some of the improvements we’ve made to the campaign:

[h1]Demo[/h1]
First of all to reward you for waiting we've decided to add a demo access as an additional Kickstarter reward! :) We will send out the demo keys just after the end of the campaign! So if you decide to become our backer you will be able to try out Soulblight really soon!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/d16bd87eb8e16bbd309bfaa36035b5223c91e8e1.png[/img]

[h1]New Main Message[/h1]
One of the main reasons for postponing Kickstarter was the fact that our “More literal approach to RPG” pitch was a bit too abstract to get across without at least two paragraphs of text. However removing this aspect from the game to make it more “promotable” was absolutely out of the question. The only solution was finding a new way of talking about our game. The answer came to us at PAX West. While chatting with all the people visiting our stand we’ve realized that we’ve been focusing on a wrong thing in our pitch. Instead of talking about game’s mechanics we should be emphasizing what we’re actually trying to say with it.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/16cf450b094c60d9f06282e6b424acded5ed2f34.png[/img]

Probably some of you already know what I’m talking about :). The question: [i]“Why the personalities you can acquire in the game are always negative?”[/i] was popping out quite regularly. It was natural as all the little signs were already there:
[list]
[*]The name of the game - “Soulblight” suggest that it’s about the sickness of the soul
[*]The quote form “The Divine Comedy” in the trailer pointed in this direction as well
[*]Our main art presenting that the greatest danger in the game will come “from behind you”
[*]The fact that we chose to call progression system in the game “Taining Mechanic” was also a hint
[/list]
All this was already there. What was lacking were three sentences with which we could explain all that to the person that knows absolutely nothing about the game. (btw never thought writing 3 sentences can be that hard) And so here it is:

[b][i]Soulblight is a dark, top-down roguelike luring you to cross the thin line between good and evil. Embrace your flaws to survive a journey through an unforgiving Sanctuary. Gluttony, Lust, Cannibalism - how far are you willing to go?[/i][/b]

[h1]New Main Art[/h1]
Another thing we’ve addressed was our main art. It wasn’t that we weren't satisfied with the one we had. On the contrary we really liked how straightforward it presented the top down perspective and at the same time shown the danger of Soulblight lurking behind the character. The thing that we considered a problem was the fact that once you scaled it down its readability dropped drastically. This unfortunately was a deal breaker as most of the time the art will be viewed in a crowded social media feed. And so we’ve decided to prepare a new one. This time focusing on the character and it’s transformation into something evil.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/58b62898439544daa6d287715c3a1cc495ab3617.png[/img]

notes.title: Soulblight Alpha Demo Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26308370/10587c3ec03b8b6d53c36bd46e05604e082393d2.png[/img]
One of you (Edwin) suggested that I would post the Alpha Update change logs here to help you all follow on the development. This is an Awesome idea. Not sure why I haven't thought about it earlier :P It happens that I just uploaded new update so here comes the first one:

[list]
[*]The alpha build is now in the form of Kickstarter Demo. It's a bit shorter as we don't want to show the locations that still contain assets in a concept stage(like camp and chapel)
[*]Chrono Inhibitor armor set added. Armor of this type allows you to use time slowing mechanic. 
[*]Spiked armor set added. Armor deals passive damage to the enemy when in Grip.
[*]First light armor set added.
[*]Items made of black steel can no longer kill you. When you equip an item with that tag while on full wounds you simply don't receive the Black Steel Curse buff until you heal.
[*]6 light shields added
[*]6 medium shields added
[*]6 heavy shields added
[*]Spear primary attack speed has been increased. This weapon type seemed to be a bit under-powered.
[*]The loot you receive as a taint reward is now more varied.
[*]Bosses movement speed increased. You should no longer be able to infinity kite him. 
[*]Now when you’re sneaking through the creaking zone the range in which the sound is heard depends on how fast you're walking (You can sneak slower by gently moving the analog stick)
[/list]

P.S
If you'r interested in checking out Soulblight sign up for the alpha demo at www.mynextgames.com
You can also  support our upcoming kickstarter. it goes live on AUG 17th here's the thunderclap link: https://www.thunderclap.it/projects/59652-soulblight-live-on-kickstarter
